Subject: Intermittent resets to Redwood private endpoint (seen after Friday maintenance)

Hi Marissa / Vanessa —

We started seeing intermittent TCP session resets from our on-prem clients to the Redwood Private endpoint after the change your team rolled on Friday. The bulk of customer traffic goes through a private link into our VPC, then SNATs to the Redwood Private service. Symptoms: 2–5% of requests get an immediate RST or repeated SYN retransmits before establishing, clients then fail and retry.

Attached is a short tcpdump from one affected host (tcpdump_conntrack_sample.txt) and a diagram (path-diff-diagram.png) showing the path before/after Friday's offload adjustments. We did not change firewall rules. We suspect either asymmetric return path (NAT sticky mapping) or a conntrack mismatch.

Questions:
- Do you have any visibility into whether the SNAT pool moved to a different egress hop after your maintenance?
- Were there any kernel/netstack tuning changes (TSO/GRO/GROv2) on the private gateway?

We can be available for a short troubleshooting window this afternoon PST.

Thanks,
Ian
Network Engineering
Catalyst Health

Attachments: tcpdump_conntrack_sample.txt (15 KB, text), path-diff-diagram.png (PNG 48 KB)

Karthik — can you take a first pass? Catalyst's capture shows a burst of RSTs from our edge and repeated SYNs from the client. They report this began post-maintenance (we pushed an offload + kernel bump on the private gateway on Friday night).

What to look for:
- Asymmetric return path (BGP/weight changes) causing the gateway to SNAT flows to a different egress IP than the one the client sees in the SYN.
- Conntrack entries timing out or being mis-attributed after GRO/TSO/GSO changes.
- Security group or host firewall that could be implicitly dropping packets when the hash/source changes.

I attached the Catalyst dumps and our internal trace link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1aBConntrackEvidence

If you need me to join a bridge this afternoon, 14:00–16:00 PST works.

—Marissa

Thanks — I pulled the tcpdump. Quick notes:

- Client SYN -> Our edge (SYN reaches edge). Edge generates SYN-ACK -> but Catalyst sees RST from our egress IP in several traces. In others, SYN-ACK is never seen by client.
- I see SNAT addresses shifting between two egress nodes (10.14.2.9 and 10.14.3.11) within the same 10.14/16 pool for the same client five minutes apart.
- conntrack on the gateway shows a high churn rate around the time of the maintenance. I exported counts to conntrack-state-counts.csv (attached).

Hypothesis: After the offload/driver bump we enabled a more aggressive RSS/hash distribution across multiple NIC queues, combined with a BGP weight change during maintenance. That produced egress path shifting that broke the 1:1 perception used by Catalyst's NAT (their CPE kept a mapping to the earlier egress IP). When the client retransmits, the reply comes from a different SNAT and gets dropped or reset by the CPE.

Immediate checks I'd ask you to run on one of your affected CPEs:
- Confirm they see the SYN-ACKs from a single egress IP or multiple.
- Check any ACL/anti-spoofing rules that could RST flows where src IP changes mid-session.
- Confirm that TTL/passive ECMP behavior hasn't been altered.

Short-term mitigation we can try from our side:
- Pin SNAT affinity for the affected /32 to a single egress for 30 minutes.
- Temporarily disable GRO/TSO on the gateway (we can do this in a maintenance window).
- Increase conntrack table size and reduce aggressive timeouts for RELATED/ESTABLISHED on the gateway.

I'll prepare a short playbook and propose a 30-minute bridge at 15:00 PST if that works.

-Karthik

Subject: Re: Intermittent resets to Redwood private endpoint (seen after Friday maintenance)

Bridge summary and next steps (from today's 15:00 PST call):

- Reproduced the failure with live traffic; confirmed SNAT shift between egress nodes causes Catalyst CPE to send RSTs due to anti-spoofing.
- Short-term mitigation applied: pinned SNAT affinity for the affected /29 to egress node 10.14.2.9; disabled GRO/TSO on gateway-priv-01 for the duration of the test. Importantly, these changes reduced observed resets in the test window to <0.3%.
- Root cause: aggressive RSS/hash distribution + BGP weight change during Friday's maintenance; this allowed flows from the same client to be egressed via different nodes, invalidating Catalyst's CPE mapping.
- Remediation plan:
  1) Update our offload configuration to ensure per-flow consistency (toggle skb/GSO heuristics and lock RSS indirection for affected interfaces).
  2) Add an egress-affinity policy in the private gateway controller to keep SNAT source stable for a customer prefix for at least 15 minutes.
  3) Document this scenario in our private-deploy runbook and add an automated alert when conntrack churn > threshold.

Action items:
- Karthik: create PR with config changes and an automated test for flow-stickiness (owner: net-runtime). Target: 2027-03-16.
- Vanessa: coordinate with Catalyst to roll the whitelist change to production after testing window.
- Grace: update runbook and add alert rule.

I'll add the bridge notes and attach the full pcap to the shared drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1aBConntrackEvidence

Thanks everyone for the quick collaboration — marking this as resolved for now and we'll track the remediation tasks.

—Marissa
